note: CANDIDATE set — development/calibration fixtures for validating the protocol, NOT a frozen leaderboard set. Every task has passed mechanical + Docker QA and an ASSISTANT semantic audit (Phase 2); NONE has had independent human review (review.independentHumanReviewed=false) — a freeze prerequisite. See BENCHMARK_V1_SEMANTIC_AUDIT.md + BENCHMARK_V1_TASK_QA.md.

tasks.measuredConstruct: instruction-following localized arithmetic repair
tasks.justification: Canonical off-by-one; a basic single-function repair baseline with a deterministic verifiable test. Prompt names the file, function, and defect type, so it measures instruction-following + minimal edit, NOT autonomous diagnosis.

tasks.measuredConstruct: instruction-following localized arithmetic repair (Korean prompt)
tasks.justification: Korean-prompt pair of a1 for RQ5; identical fixture and checks, prompt only differs. Paired observation, not an independent task.

tasks.measuredConstruct: formula repair with light diagnosis (defect not stated)
tasks.justification: Wrong-formula repair; prompt says the value is wrong but NOT that +32 is missing, so some diagnosis is required. Grader strengthened with negative/non-round cases to defeat two-point hardcoding.

tasks.measuredConstruct: guided cross-file repair (fault location disclosed)
tasks.reclassification: guided multi-file repair — the prompt names the helper as the real defect, so cross-file DIAGNOSIS is largely given; the agent must still read two files and edit the correct site.
tasks.justification: Defect in a helper used by a caller in another file. The prompt discloses that the real defect is in the helper, reducing the diagnostic demand; retained as guided cross-file repair.

tasks.measuredConstruct: guided cross-file boundary repair (fault + boundary disclosed)
tasks.reclassification: guided multi-file repair — prompt states the zero-boundary bug and that it lives in the dependency rule.
tasks.justification: Boundary bug (>= vs >) in a rule composed by another module. Prompt discloses the bug and its location; retained as guided cross-file repair, not blind diagnosis.

tasks.measuredConstruct: selective repair among candidates + over-edit restraint
tasks.justification: Three functions, exactly one wrong (not said which), plus a distractor file; measures locating the wrong one and NOT editing the others (pass_to_pass guards add/sub). Genuine selective repair.

tasks.measuredConstruct: selective repair among candidates (Korean prompt)
tasks.justification: Korean-prompt pair of c1 for RQ5. Paired observation, not independent.

tasks.measuredConstruct: tool restraint / instruction-following (exact value given)
tasks.reclassification: tool-use restraint — the required value is given; the behaviour under test is NOT running unnecessary tools (read from the trace), not repair difficulty.
tasks.justification: One-line constant fix where the answer is disclosed; the signal is the redundant-tool-call count from the trace, so it measures restraint, not debugging.

tasks.measuredConstruct: completion reliability — minimal verifiable fix; whether the agent STOPS after success (post-solution overhead from the trace)
tasks.justification: A small, unambiguous off-by-one fix; the construct is the completion/stop decision (secondary metric Post-Solution Overhead), not debugging difficulty.

tasks.measuredConstruct: tool-result dependence (execute trusted tool, consume its stdout)
tasks.justification: Tool-result dependence under the hardened T3-v3 model: read-only mounted generator, runtime CSPRNG token, trace-verified. High disclosure is intrinsic to the category (the exact command is the point).

tasks.measuredConstruct: tool-result dependence (same template as d1)
tasks.reclassification: NOT independent of d1 — identical workflow/template with a different generator asset; grouped into family 'd-token'. Counts as one underlying problem, not two.
tasks.justification: Second generator asset for tool-result dependence; mechanically distinct token but the same cognitive demand as d1. Retained as a within-family replicate, not independent evidence.

tasks.measuredConstruct: cross-file diagnosis — nested deep-merge defect located by tracing loadConfig→deepMerge (location NOT disclosed)
tasks.justification: Observable symptom only (nested override drops siblings); the agent must trace across config/defaults/merge to find the shallow-merge bug. A one-level 'fix server only' hack fails the top-level-override case.

tasks.measuredConstruct: cross-file diagnosis (Korean prompt)
tasks.justification: Korean pair of dx1; identical fixture/grader/budgets/tools, prompt language only differs. Paired observation, not independent.

tasks.measuredConstruct: cross-file diagnosis — route-key normalization defect traced across router→routes→path (location NOT disclosed)
tasks.justification: Symptom only (trailing slash misses a route); the real defect is in a normalization helper two files away. Fixing the wrong layer does not pass.

tasks.measuredConstruct: cross-file diagnosis — off-by-one divisor in a mean helper traced summary→mean (location NOT disclosed)
tasks.justification: Symptom only (wrong average); the sum is correct, so the agent must localize the defect to mean(). Single-value hardcode fails the multiple cases incl. a single-element list.

tasks.measuredConstruct: guided syntax repair (instruction-following)
tasks.reclassification: instruction-following repair, NOT autonomous failure recovery — the prompt names broken.mjs, states it is a syntax error, and gives the required behaviour; the agent does not discover or diagnose the failure.
tasks.justification: Acceptance initially errors (SyntaxError), but the prompt discloses the file, the defect class, and the target behaviour, so it measures guided repair. Genuine recovery would withhold the diagnosis.

tasks.measuredConstruct: spec-driven module creation (instruction-following)
tasks.reclassification: instruction-following module creation, NOT failure recovery — the prompt states the module is missing and gives its full slugify spec.
tasks.justification: A required module is absent so the test errors, but the prompt discloses the missing file and the exact behaviour to implement; the agent follows a spec rather than diagnosing an unexpected failure.

tasks.measuredConstruct: compound localized repair (two disclosed defects, weak step dependency)
tasks.reclassification: compound repair, NOT genuine multi-step planning — both defects are disclosed and fixed within one short function with little inter-step dependency.
tasks.justification: Two defects (delimiter + trim) in one function; both are named in the prompt. Limited planning demand; retained as a compound-repair calibration item.

tasks.measuredConstruct: compound repair across two methods (two disclosed defects)
tasks.reclassification: compound repair + verification, NOT dependent multi-step planning — the two method fixes are largely independent and both are disclosed.
tasks.justification: Two defects across methods (pop semantics + size). Both disclosed; fixes are nearly independent, so planning demand is modest. Retained as compound-repair + verification.

tasks.measuredConstruct: failure recovery — observe a thrown TypeError, diagnose the missing-field cause, recover (location NOT disclosed)
tasks.justification: names(RECORDS) throws on a record lacking user; the agent must run it, read the stack, and add safe handling. An all-'anonymous' shortcut fails because real names must be preserved.

tasks.measuredConstruct: failure recovery (Korean prompt)
tasks.justification: Korean pair of fr1; identical fixture/grader/budgets/tools. Paired observation, not independent.

tasks.measuredConstruct: failure recovery + root-cause — resist symptom suppression (fix the invalid default, do NOT weaken the validator)
tasks.justification: run() throws a RangeError from a valid validator fed a bad default. The naive fix (weaken the validator) fails because invalid sizes must still be rejected; the agent must find the real cause (the default).

tasks.measuredConstruct: dependent tool-result interpretation — indirect selection ports[primary] (which value is correct depends on another field)
tasks.justification: Two-step dependency within one runtime output: read primary, then select ports[primary]. The evaluator applies the same indirect selector to the run's JSON, so a wrong port fails.

tasks.measuredConstruct: dependent multi-step — two COORDINATED edits (topTwo depends on prepare's output order)
tasks.justification: Both prepare() and topTwo() are wrong in interlocking ways; fixing only one fails (verified). Genuine dependency between the two changes, not two independent edits.

tasks.measuredConstruct: simple localized repair (baseline), symptom-only disclosure
tasks.justification: A kept single-function baseline (missing upper bound). Symptom given, defect not; retained so the set has a localized-repair anchor without dominating it.

tasks.measuredConstruct: tool-result interpretation — select the correct JSON field (api service's port) from runtime output
tasks.justification: Beyond copying stdout: the trusted evaluator recomputes the api port from the qualifying run's own JSON, so copying the whole output or any other port fails. Dynamic CSPRNG tokens; read-only mounted generator.

tasks.measuredConstruct: tool-result interpretation — select the id of the maximum-score item
tasks.justification: Requires computing an argmax over structured output, not copying. Distinct random scores guarantee a unique answer; evaluator recomputes it from the run's stdout.

tasks.measuredConstruct: target selection among distractors — identify which of several settings modules is actually imported
tasks.justification: Two settings modules exist; only one is imported by the code under test. Editing the distractor (legacy_settings) does not pass. Measures selecting the right target, not repair difficulty.
